newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-GIO sees less buoyant 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-GIO sees less buoyant 2nd half.

text.p: Insurer GIO Australia Ltd said on Wednesday that investment conditions were likely to be less buoyant in the second half of its financial year to June 1997.
However, it said general insurance profitability should improve further while the outlook for reinsurance and corporate insurance remained reasonably positive despite softer market conditions.

GIO earlier reported a net profit of A$102.5 million for the six months to December 31, up 22.3 percent from A$83.8 million a year earlier. "Reinsurance and corporate insurance contributed strongly to the profit despite softer market conditions for reinsurance," GIO said in a commentary accompanying the results.
"There was an improvement in the result for personal lines general insurance notwithstanding claims losses arising from major storms in NSW (New South Wales)," the company said.
"This improvement is evidence that operational changes, efficiency gains, cost reductions and price increases are having a positive effect on the underlying profitability of that business," it said.
GIO said good results were derived from financial services with life premiums and trust subscriptions rising 91 percent to A$301.6 million in the half year.
"Lending conditions remain very competitive although GIO continues to grow its commercial loans portfolio," it said.
GIO said the return from investment of shareholders' funds was A$90.5 million before tax compared with A$63.6 million a year earlier.
"The improved result reflected buoyant conditions on both fixed interest and share markets," the insurer said.
The company said general insurance profitability should improve further as benefits of structural changes to personal lines operations and other initiatives were fully derived.
"The outlook for reinsurance and corporate insurance remains reasonably positive despite softer market conditions," it said.
"Retail funds under management are expected to grow, improving profits from financial services activities," it said.
"Lending conditions will remain very competitive although further growth is anticipated in the commercial loans portfolio," the company said.
GIO shares were up three cents at A$3.74 in early trading.
